content_html:
One original print, every morning.

A thermal receipt printer in my kitchen wakes up each day and prints a piece of character art that has never existed before, designed minutes earlier by Claude, themed to the day: the weather outside, the season, whatever the news feels like. A short verse underneath. One physical copy, 80mm wide, and that is the whole broadcast.

Two mornings, a day apart. Most days stand on their own; once in a while a piece answers the one before it, the way July 4 answered July 3 above.

This started as a bet against my phone. The first minutes of the day kept going to feeds, so I pointed the same inputs at a printer instead. It reads what the feeds read (forecasts, anniversaries, and the day's headlines when it goes looking for them) and hands back one finished thing you can hold. There is nothing to refresh; when the cutter drops, the day's edition is out. Yesterday's goes up on the corkboard.

The cloud half is a single Google Apps Script. The only hardware on my side is a Raspberry Pi Zero W running a small Python bridge (systemd plus an ngrok tunnel; runbook in docs/) that pipes bytes into the printer's USB port.

How it works

graph LR
  subgraph cloud["Google Apps Script · daily trigger"]
    A(["daily brief"]) --> B["Claude designs<br/>an art spec"] --> C["render to<br/>ESC/POS"]
  end
  subgraph kitchen["the kitchen"]
    D["Pi Zero W"] --> E(["Epson prints<br/>and cuts"])
  end
  C -- "POST · ngrok ·<br/>basic auth" --> D
Loading
  1. Context. printDailyArt() (src/art.ts) builds a small brief: today's date, the season, current weather from the Google Weather API, and a rolling archive of the last 14 pieces (title + one-line style note each).
  2. Design. Claude gets a system prompt describing the medium (a 48-column monospace grid, 1-bit black, only CP437, the old IBM PC character set) and is asked for one committed idea that differs sharply from everything in the archive. On a day that genuinely earns it (a holiday after its eve, an event still unfolding, a resonant anniversary) it may instead answer an earlier piece; the pair at the top of this page is one of those. It can run a few web searches to feel out the day. Structured output (a JSON schema) constrains the reply to an art spec: an array of styled text ops plus a short verse.
  3. Render. A ~50-line renderer turns ops into raw ESC/POS bytes (ESC/POS is the byte-level command language receipt printers speak). No drivers, no images: the art is literally text with style commands.
  4. Print. The bytes are POSTed to the Pi, which writes them to the printer's character device. The receipt prints: a small date stamp, the artwork, the verse. Nothing else: no title, no branding.

The medium

The canvas: 203 dpi, one bit of color, 48 monospace columns, and a character set frozen in 1981. Everything the model can do, it does with CP437:

Trick How
Tone / gradients ░ ▒ ▓ █ ramps across rows
Sub-character edges half-blocks ▀ ▄ ▌ ▐ ■ for silhouettes
Solid black fields inverted (white-on-black) runs; even spaces print solid
Seamless shapes line spacing set to exactly one glyph height, so rows tile
Giant type independent width/height scaling, 1–8× each
Fine texture the printer's second font: 9×17 glyphs, 64 columns
Structure full single/double box drawing, ° · ∙ ≈ ∞ π Σ and friends

The "seamless shapes" row is the trick that makes block art possible at all: by default the printer leaves a white seam between text lines, but ESC 3 with the right value makes ░▒▓█ rows fuse into continuous fields. The value was calibrated empirically with a built-in test page. That page, and every other byte this project sends, is documented in docs/escpos-protocol.md.

The art spec

The model doesn't emit bytes; it emits a declarative spec the renderer executes. Abbreviated:

{
  "title": "GOLDEN RUN",
  "caption": "Test pattern: gradient, silhouette, invert, scale, texture.",
  "verse": "The mountains hold their breath;\nthe sun tries every shade of gray\nbefore committing to gold.",
  "style": "calibration plate; gradient + silhouette + type specimen",
  "continues": "",
  "ops": [
    { "text": "░░░░…\n▒▒▒▒…\n▓▓▓▓…", "gapless": true },
    { "text": " DAWN ", "width": 2, "height": 2, "bold": true, "invert": true },
    { "text": "every feature · one receipt", "font": "B", "align": "right" }
  ]
}

Only the artwork and the verse are printed. The rest are archive fields: the title and style land in a rolling ART_HISTORY property that the next day's prompt receives as a list to differ from; the caption goes to the execution log only. That pressure keeps a daily generative loop from collapsing into the same sunset every morning, and the prompt pushes rotation across the whole space: landscapes, geometric abstraction, pattern studies, giant-type posters, constellation maps, weather glyphs, emblems, diagrams.

continues is the deliberate exception. It stays empty almost every day, but when the day itself hands the model a thread (the Fourth of July arriving after its eve, an event still unfolding, a tenth anniversary), the model may build on one recent piece and record which. Those links show up as markers in the history it reads on later days, and a fresh marker raises the bar for the next one. That is what keeps continuations a surprise instead of a habit.

The renderer treats the spec as untrusted: sizes are clamped, rows are truncated to the column budget, control characters are stripped, output is capped at 150 rows (~45cm of paper), and anything CP437 can't print becomes a visible-but-harmless ?.

Structured output guarantees the shape of the JSON, not the size of the strings inside it, and one run in July 2026 found that gap: valid JSON with a 3,155-character title of repeated filler. The archive saved it, every later prompt replayed it, and the model learned its own loop; within a week the receipt was a page of the model talking to itself instead of artwork. Specs are now checked against the length bounds the schema describes before anything is printed or written to the archive; a rejected spec throws to the alert email, and the next trigger retries. The archive is sanitized on read too, so an already poisoned entry is dropped once instead of fed back for fourteen days.

A few API notes, for the curious: the art spec comes back via structured output (output_config.format with a JSON schema), and web search runs as a server-side tool, so the client just resumes on stop_reason: "pause_turn". The local harness enables the server-side fallback beta (another model re-serves a refused request); the production path does not, so a refusal there fails loudly to the alert email. Details in CLAUDE.md.

Hardware

  • Printer: Epson TM-T20III, an 80mm ESC/POS thermal printer with an auto-cutter. Any ESC/POS printer with a CP437 code page should work after recalibrating the column constants (node test-print.mjs ruler).
  • Bridge: Raspberry Pi Zero W running a ~40-line Python http.server that writes request bodies straight to /dev/usb/lp0, exposed through an ngrok static domain with basic auth, kept alive by systemd. The script itself lives on the Pi and is not committed here; its whole contract is "write each POST body to /dev/usb/lp0", and the runbook covers the rest.

The full byte-level protocol (every command, the CP437 mapping, the geometry and calibration results) is specced in docs/escpos-protocol.md. The Pi's setup, maintenance, troubleshooting, and disaster recovery live in docs/pi-print-server-runbook.md.

Run your own

You need an ESC/POS printer, something that can pipe bytes to its USB port (here, a Pi Zero W; see Hardware and the runbook), an ngrok static domain, an Anthropic API key, a Google account for Apps Script, and Node for the build.

TypeScript under src/ is the source of truth; esbuild bundles it to a single dist/main.gs, which clasp pushes to Apps Script.

npm install        # dev tooling: clasp, typescript, esbuild, prettier
npm run build      # tsc --noEmit + esbuild bundle -> dist/main.gs
npm run status     # list the files clasp would push (dry check)
npm run push       # build, then clasp push (uploads dist/)

The Apps Script web editor is a mirror, not a second source of truth: edit locally and push. npm run pull fetches remote back down if the editor was touched directly.

First-time setup on a new machine: npx clasp login (writes ~/.clasprc.json), then npm run push. The committed .clasp.json binds to my script; for your own deployment, run npx clasp create --type standalone --rootDir dist (or put your own scriptId in .clasp.json) before the first push.

Configuration

No secrets live in the repo. Runtime config is read from Script Properties (Apps Script editor → Project Settings → Script Properties):

Property Required What it is
PI_URL yes ngrok HTTPS URL of the Pi print bridge
NGROK_USER yes basic-auth username for the tunnel
NGROK_PASS yes basic-auth password for the tunnel
ANTHROPIC_KEY yes Anthropic API key (claude-fable-5)
EMAIL_ALERTS_TO no where failure alerts are emailed (rate-limited)
GEMINI_KEY no Google API key for the Weather API
LAT / LON no location for weather context

Weather is garnish, not a dependency: without GEMINI_KEY/LAT/LON the art still prints, just uninformed about the sky.

State keys managed by the script itself (no setup): LAST_ART_DATE (one art print per day), ART_HISTORY (the rolling archive fed back into the prompt, with markers on pieces that continued an earlier one), and LAST_ALERT_TIME (rate-limits alert emails).

Trigger

Create one time-driven trigger on printDailyArt (Apps Script editor → Triggers). A morning hour works well. An hourly trigger is also safe: LAST_ART_DATE limits it to one print per day, and because the guard is only set on success, extra runs double as retries after a failure.

testDailyArt() prints the golden test plate (no API call) to verify the hardware path. Set DRY_RUN = true in src/art.ts to log specs instead of printing.

Local iteration

test-print.mjs sends ESC/POS straight to the Pi bridge (the same endpoint Apps Script hits), so you can iterate without deploying or waiting on a trigger. The art modes load the real builders from the built dist/main.gs, so run npm run build first; the preview then matches production exactly.

cp .env.example .env            # then fill in PI_URL / NGROK_USER / NGROK_PASS
npm run build                   # needed for modes that load dist/main.gs
node test-print.mjs hello       # minimal "SYSTEM ONLINE" connectivity test
node test-print.mjs text "Hi"   # arbitrary text
node test-print.mjs ruler       # column + gapless-spacing calibration page
node test-print.mjs art         # golden art spec through the real renderer (no API)
node test-print.mjs art:live    # LIVE end-to-end art (ANTHROPIC_KEY in .env)
node test-print.mjs art --dry   # print the hex payload instead of sending

This script is local only; it isn't bundled into dist/ or pushed to Apps Script.

Contributing

Clone the repo, npm install, and start Claude Code in the root; it picks up CLAUDE.md automatically, which carries the architecture, the deploy ritual, and the byte-level gotchas. You can iterate on the renderer with no hardware at all: node test-print.mjs art --dry shows the exact ESC/POS bytes a change produces. The longer version, including a good first prompt to hand Claude, is in CONTRIBUTING.md.

Layout

src/
  appsscript.json   manifest (V8, America/Los_Angeles)
  escpos.ts         CMD command table, column constants, encodeCP437
  art.ts            the daily art job: prompt, schema, renderer, Anthropic client
  transport.ts      sendToPi (HTTP → Pi bridge), retries, alert emails
  weather.ts        Google Weather API fetcher (context for the prompt)
  main.ts           entry points re-exported for the build footer
build.js            esbuild bundle → dist/main.gs
test-print.mjs      local print harness (talks to the Pi directly)
docs/
  escpos-protocol.md         the full byte-level protocol spec
  pi-print-server-runbook.md the Pi side: setup, ops, troubleshooting
example/
  example_1.jpeg             the Liberty Bell piece, fresh off the printer
  example_2.jpeg             the Jul 3 -> Jul 4 sequence, pinned side by side

clasp uploads only dist/ (.clasp.json → "rootDir": "dist"), which is gitignored.

blocks.html_en: • Design. Claude gets a system prompt describing the medium (a 48-column monospace grid, 1-bit black, only CP437, the old IBM PC character set) and is asked for one committed idea that differs sharply from everything in the archive. blocks.html_en: Structured output guarantees the shape of the JSON, not the size of the strings inside it, and one run in July 2026 found that gap: valid JSON with a 3,155-character title of repeated filler. The archive saved it, every later prompt replayed it, and the model learned its own loop; within a week the receipt was a page of the model talking to itself instead of artwork. Specs are now checked against the length bounds the schema describes before anything is printed or written to the archive; a rejected spec throws to the alert email, and the next trigger retries. The archive is sanitized on read too, so an already poisoned entry is dropped once instead of fed back for fourteen days.

blocks.html_en: A few API notes, for the curious: the art spec comes back via structured output (output_config.format with a JSON schema), and web search runs as a server-side tool, so the client just resumes on stop_reason: "pause_turn". content_html_zh:
每天早上一张原创印刷品。

我厨房里的热敏收据打印机每天都会醒来，打印出一幅以前从未存在过的人物艺术作品，由克劳德在几分钟前设计，主题是当天的：外面的天气，季节，无论新闻感觉如何。 底下有一小段诗句。 一份实体副本，80 毫米宽，这就是整个广播。

两个早上，相隔一天。 大多数日子都是独立的；偶尔会有一篇文章回答前一篇文章，就像上面的 7 月 4 日回答 7 月 3 日一样。

这始于对我的手机的赌注。 当天的头几分钟一直在进行提要，因此我将相同的输入指向打印机。 它会读取提要所读取的内容（预测、周年纪念日以及寻找时的当天头条新闻），然后将一件完成的东西交还给您。 没有什么可以刷新的；当刀具落下时，当天的版本就结束了。 昨天的内容出现在软木板上。

云的一半是一个单一的 Google Apps 脚本。 我这边唯一的硬件是 Raspberry Pi Zero W，运行一个小型 Python 桥（systemd 加上 ngrok 隧道；文档/中的运行手册），将字节通过管道传输到打印机的 USB 端口。

它是如何运作的

graph LR
  subgraph cloud["Google Apps Script · daily trigger"]
    A(["daily brief"]) --> B["Claude designs<br/>an art spec"] --> C["render to<br/>ESC/POS"]
  end
  subgraph kitchen["the kitchen"]
    D["Pi Zero W"] --> E(["Epson prints<br/>and cuts"])
  end
  C -- "POST · ngrok ·<br/>basic auth" --> D
Loading
  1. 语境。 printDailyArt() (src/art.ts) 构建一个小摘要：今天的日期、季节、来自 Google Weather API 的当前天气，以及最后 14 篇文章的滚动存档（标题 + 每行注释）。
  2. 设计。 Claude 收到一个描述介质的系统提示（48 列等宽网格，1 位黑色，只有 CP437，旧的 IBM PC 字符集），并被要求提供一个与档案中的所有内容截然不同的承诺想法。 在真正值得的一天（前夕之后的假期，仍在展开的事件，引起共鸣的周年纪念日），它可能会回答较早的作品；本页顶部的一对就是其中之一。 它可以运行一些网络搜索来感受这一天。 结构化输出（JSON 模式）限制对艺术规范的回复：一组样式化的文本操作加上一段简短的诗句。
  3. 使成为。 大约 50 行渲染器将操作转换为原始 ESC/POS 字节（ESC/POS 是收据打印机使用的字节级命令语言）。 没有驱动程序，没有图像：艺术实际上是带有样式命令的文本。
  4. 打印。 这些字节被 POST 到 Pi，Pi 将它们写入打印机的字符设备。 收据上印有：小日期印章、艺术品、诗句。 没有别的：没有标题，没有品牌。

媒介

画布：203 dpi、一点颜色、48 个等宽列以及 1981 年冻结的字符集。 该模型可以做的所有事情，都可以通过 CP437 完成：

Trick How
色调/渐变 ░ ▒ ▓ █ 跨行坡道
子字符边缘 半块 ▀ ▄ ▌ ▐ ■ 用于剪影
纯黑场 反转（黑底白字）运行；均匀的空格打印为实心
无缝形状 行间距恰好设置为一个字形高度，因此行平铺
巨人型 独立的宽度/高度缩放，每个 1–8×
质地细腻 打印机的第二种字体：9×17 字形，64 列
结构 完整的单/双方框图，° · ∙ ≈ ∞ π Σ 和朋友

“无缝形状”行是使块艺术成为可能的技巧：默认情况下，打印机在文本行之间留下白色接缝，但具有正确值的 ESC 3 使 ░▒▓█ 行融合成连续字段。 该值是通过内置测试页根据经验进行校准的。 该页面以及该项目发送的每个其他字节都记录在 docs/escpos-protocol.md 中。

艺术规格

该模型不发出字节；它发出渲染器执行的声明性规范。 缩写：

{
  "title": "GOLDEN RUN",
  "caption": "Test pattern: gradient, silhouette, invert, scale, texture.",
  "verse": "The mountains hold their breath;\nthe sun tries every shade of gray\nbefore committing to gold.",
  "style": "calibration plate; gradient + silhouette + type specimen",
  "continues": "",
  "ops": [
    { "text": "░░░░…\n▒▒▒▒…\n▓▓▓▓…", "gapless": true },
    { "text": " DAWN ", "width": 2, "height": 2, "bold": true, "invert": true },
    { "text": "every feature · one receipt", "font": "B", "align": "right" }
  ]
}

仅印刷艺术品和诗句。 其余的是存档字段：标题和样式位于滚动的 ART_HISTORY 属性中，第二天的提示会以列表形式接收到该属性以区别；标题仅进入执行日志。 这种压力使每天的生成循环不会崩溃成每天早上的同一个日落，而提示则推动整个空间的旋转：风景、几何抽象、图案研究、巨型海报、星座图、天气字形、标志、图表。

继续是故意的例外。 它几乎每天都是空的，但是当这一天本身给模型带来一条线索时（七月四日在其前夜之后到来，一个事件仍在展开，十周年纪念日），模型可能会以最近的一件作品为基础并记录下来。 这些链接在以后读取的历史记录中显示为标记，新的标记提高了下一个标记的标准。 这就是为什么连续性会让人感到惊讶，而不是成为一种习惯。

渲染器将​​规范视为不受信任：大小被限制，行被截断为列预算，控制字符被剥离，输出上限为 150 行（约 45 厘米的纸张），任何 CP437 无法打印的内容都会变成可见但无害的 ?。

结构化输出保证了 JSON 的形状，而不是其中字符串的大小，2026 年 7 月的一次运行发现了这一差距：有效的 JSON 具有 3,155 个字符的重复填充标题。 存档保存了它，以后的每个提示都会重播它，并且模型学习了自己的循环；一周之内，收据就变成了模型的一页自言自语，而不是艺术品。 现在，在打印任何内容或将其写入存档之前，会根据模式描述的长度范围检查规格；被拒绝的规范会发送到警报电子邮件，并重试下一个触发器。 存档在读取时也会进行清理，因此已经中毒的条目会被删除一次，而不是在十四天内反馈。

一些 API 注释，出于好奇：艺术规范通过结构化输出（具有 JSON 模式的 output_config.format）返回，并且 Web 搜索作为服务器端工具运行，因此客户端只需在 stop_reason:“pause_turn”上恢复。 本地线束启用服务器端回退测试版（另一个模型重新服务被拒绝的请求）；生产路径没有，因此拒绝会严重影响警报电子邮件。 详细信息请参见 CLAUDE.md。

硬件

  • 打印机：Epson TM-T20III，80mm ESC/POS 热敏打印机，带自动切纸器。 任何具有 CP437 代码页的 ESC/POS 打印机在重新校准列常数（节点 test-print.mjs 标尺）后都应该可以工作。
  • Bridge：Raspberry Pi Zero W 运行约 40 行的 Python http.server，将请求主体直接写入 /dev/usb/lp0，通过具有基本身份验证的 ngrok 静态域公开，由 systemd 保持活动状态。 脚本本身存在于 Pi 上，并不在这里提交；它的整个合同是“将每个 POST 正文写入 /dev/usb/lp0”，并且 Runbook 涵盖了其余部分。

完整的字节级协议（每个命令、CP437 映射、几何和校准结果）在 docs/escpos-protocol.md 中指定。 Pi 的设置、维护、故障排除和灾难恢复位于 docs/pi-print-server-runbook.md 中。

运行你自己的

您需要一台 ESC/POS 打印机、一个可以通过管道将字节传输到其 USB 端口的设备（此处为 Pi Zero W；请参阅硬件和运行手册）、一个 ngrok 静态域、一个 Anthropic API 密钥、一个用于 Apps 脚本的 Google 帐户以及用于构建的 Node。

src/下的TypeScript是事实来源； esbuild 将其捆绑到单个 dist/main.gs，该 clasp 推送到 Apps 脚本。

npm install        # dev tooling: clasp, typescript, esbuild, prettier
npm run build      # tsc --noEmit + esbuild bundle -> dist/main.gs
npm run status     # list the files clasp would push (dry check)
npm run push       # build, then clasp push (uploads dist/)

Apps 脚本 Web 编辑器是一面镜子，而不是第二个事实来源：本地编辑和推送。 如果直接触摸编辑器，则 npm run pull 将远程获取回来。

在新机器上首次设置：npx clasp login（写入 ~/.clasprc.json），然后 npm run push。 提交的 .clasp.json 绑定到我的脚本；对于您自己的部署，请在第一次推送之前运行 npx clasp create --typestandalone --rootDir dist （或将您自己的 scriptId 放入 .clasp.json 中）。

配置

仓库中没有秘密。 运行时配置从脚本属性中读取（Apps 脚本编辑器 → 项目设置 → 脚本属性）：

财产 必需的 它是什么
PI_URL yes ngrok Pi 打印桥的 HTTPS URL
NGROK_USER yes 隧道的基本身份验证用户名
NGROK_PASS yes 隧道的基本身份验证密码
ANTHROPIC_KEY yes 人类 API 密钥 (claude-fable-5)
EMAIL_ALERTS_TO no 通过电子邮件发送故障警报（速率有限）
GEMINI_KEY no 天气 API 的 Google API 密钥
纬度/经度 no 天气背景的位置

天气是装饰，而不是依赖：没有 GEMINI_KEY/LAT/LON 艺术仍然打印，只是不了解天空。

由脚本本身管理的状态键（无需设置）：LAST_ART_DATE（每天一张艺术印刷品）、ART_HISTORY（反馈到提示中的滚动存档，并在继续前一个的部分上带有标记）和 LAST_ALERT_TIME（速率限制警报电子邮件）。

扳机

在 printDailyArt 上创建一个时间驱动的触发器（Apps 脚本编辑器 → 触发器）。 早上一个小时效果很好。 每小时触发也是安全的：LAST_ART_DATE 将其限制为每天一次打印，并且由于仅在成功时设置防护，因此额外的运行次数会在失败后重试。

testDailyArt() 打印黄金测试板（无 API 调用）以验证硬件路径。 在 src/art.ts 中设置 DRY_RUN = true 以记录规格而不是打印。

局部迭代

test-print.mjs 将 ESC/POS 直接发送到 Pi 桥（相同的端点 Apps 脚本命中），因此您可以进行迭代，而无需部署或等待触发器。 art 模式从构建的 dist/main.gs 加载真正的构建器，因此首先运行 npm run build；预览然后与生产完全匹配。

cp .env.example .env            # then fill in PI_URL / NGROK_USER / NGROK_PASS
npm run build                   # needed for modes that load dist/main.gs
node test-print.mjs hello       # minimal "SYSTEM ONLINE" connectivity test
node test-print.mjs text "Hi"   # arbitrary text
node test-print.mjs ruler       # column + gapless-spacing calibration page
node test-print.mjs art         # golden art spec through the real renderer (no API)
node test-print.mjs art:live    # LIVE end-to-end art (ANTHROPIC_KEY in .env)
node test-print.mjs art --dry   # print the hex payload instead of sending

该脚本仅限本地使用；它没有捆绑到 dist/ 或推送到 Apps 脚本。

贡献

克隆 repo，npm install，并在根目录中启动 Claude Code；它会自动获取 CLAUDE.md，其中包含架构、部署仪式和字节级问题。 您可以在完全没有硬件的情况下迭代渲染器：node test-print.mjs art --dry 显示更改产生的确切 ESC/POS 字节。 较长的版本，包括交给 Claude 的良好第一个提示，位于 CONTRIBUTING.md 中。

布局

src/
  appsscript.json   manifest (V8, America/Los_Angeles)
  escpos.ts         CMD command table, column constants, encodeCP437
  art.ts            the daily art job: prompt, schema, renderer, Anthropic client
  transport.ts      sendToPi (HTTP → Pi bridge), retries, alert emails
  weather.ts        Google Weather API fetcher (context for the prompt)
  main.ts           entry points re-exported for the build footer
build.js            esbuild bundle → dist/main.gs
test-print.mjs      local print harness (talks to the Pi directly)
docs/
  escpos-protocol.md         the full byte-level protocol spec
  pi-print-server-runbook.md the Pi side: setup, ops, troubleshooting
example/
  example_1.jpeg             the Liberty Bell piece, fresh off the printer
  example_2.jpeg             the Jul 3 -> Jul 4 sequence, pinned side by side
